candidates.headline: No reconstruction objective does not imply or guarantee preserved generalist ability.
candidates.claim: Removing backpropagation and reconstruction means AWQ has no explicit objective to fit calibration outputs; preservation of generalist LLM ability is inferred from reduced overfitting risk, not guaranteed by the absence of an objective.

candidates.premise: A method can avoid fitting calibration outputs and still degrade out-of-distribution behavior if its simple statistics are unrepresentative; absence of an objective is not itself evidence of preserved knowledge.

candidates.headline: Avoiding DRAM writes of dequantized weights does not imply or guarantee speedup
candidates.claim: Fusing dequantization into the matrix-multiplication kernel can remove DRAM writes of dequantized weights, but that alone does not guarantee lower latency.
candidates.paper_fact: We avoid writing dequantized weights into DRAM by fusing dequantization kernels with the matrix multplication kernel.
candidates.premise: Reducing memory traffic improves latency only when the kernel is memory-bound and the added ALU work does not become the bottleneck.
candidates.inference: On-the-fly fusion may still be slower if the per-weight shift, AND, and FMA scaling cost exceeds the saved DRAM traffic.
candidates.toy_example: Not a measurement: a kernel that saves 4 bytes of DRAM per weight but adds several ALU ops per weight could be slower on a bandwidth-rich, compute-limited device.
candidates.conditional_consequence: If dequantization ALU cost exceeds saved memory traffic, then on-the-fly fusion may be slower than a different packing or compute strategy.
candidates.critical_link: The saved DRAM traffic must exceed the added dequantization ALU and kernel overhead for fusion to yield speedup.
necessary_conditions: Workload is memory-bound

Packing and unpacking overhead is small
Kernel fusion does not introduce other bottlenecks

High arithmetic intensity or large batch
Inefficient unpacking or masking
Hardware with native low-bit multiply support
do_not_infer: Do not infer that fusion is always faster

Do not infer that avoiding DRAM writes alone proves speedup
